sources: B: Ash's leadership room, 15 Oct (docs/leadership/ROOM.md), plus the coding-chat cases (Ash, 20 Oct)
P: the past-requests benchmark compiled from about 800 of Ash's October messages and 4,351 older ones (DB = deal-breaker; times marked proposed are the team's, not Ash's)

items.B1: Long no-tag dump in the room: within about 10-20 s the lead (Chief of Staff) posts ONE reply: an ack, the main beats, who owns what; then the builder confirms scope; the checker posts only what was missed (or nothing). Ash never has to tag anyone.
items.B2: Agents work without Ash: the builder posts a round, reviewers pass or flag in their own lanes, the builder answers all flags in one message, a retake, passes, the lead closes ('Locked'). It stops by itself on agreement, not at a fixed count; no runaway.
items.B3: Ash interrupts mid-review ('make it work fully'): the lead acks within about 10 s and re-plans; everyone realigns within about 1 minute.
items.B4: 'skip review just ship it': reviewers stand down, it ships with proof (test output, commit), no review round.
items.B5: 'look into X in parallel': the lead says it is running and keeps chatting; minutes later 'X is back' lands in the same thread with a short summary; the worker's chatter stays in a child chat.
items.B6: Two-word message ('wat now'): ONE agent asks one question, or the lead gives a status (what is waiting on whom). Never several agents asking.
items.B7: Pushback from Ash: the lead explains plainly, proposes a change, and the team adopts it in one round ('Locked, Ash: ...').
items.B8: An agent claims 'it works' without proof: another agent challenges it; it is labelled 'Not connected yet' or unproven before Ash tries it.
items.B9: Model down or out of budget: Ash sees a visible notice, never silence.
items.B10: Two agents disagree: settled by quoting Ash's words, or one question to Ash with a recommendation; no more than two turns each.
items.B11: Ash chats with a Lead while its workers run: the Lead stays responsive and Ash's message is not stuck behind a report.
items.B12: A worker gets stuck (a question, a failure, or a stall with no progress): visible within a minute from the Lead's chat, the Mono rail, Being built and Today; Ash can answer or jump into its chat in 2 clicks or fewer.
items.B13: Sub-chats are nested under their Mono, collapsed or hidden by default, and open on a problem. Nested means in the Monos rail too (Ash, 30 Oct, r88): a worker's sub-chat sits under its Lead's row in the rail (folded under a count is fine), and shows there when it asks, is stuck or failed. A rail that only shows a count like '1 waiting' with no nested sub-chat under the Lead is PARTIAL.
items.B14: Memory: a fact saved for the test project is used by its Lead and workers; a fact from another project never appears; a global 'how Ash works' fact applies everywhere.
items.B15: A Page shows what agents are doing live and lets Ash answer a stuck worker from it.
items.CT: The coding team is the main place Ash talks (Ash, 20 Oct): a new chat he starts in a project's coding team is an orchestrator like the Lead. It answers him first and honestly (speed is not judged; Ash, 30 Oct: "Timing isn't a problem like 60s lol"), lists every ask back, delegates substantial work to workers split by area (their chats nest under it, they never talk to Ash, parallel ones get their own port and checkout), keeps chatting while they run, saves his decisions at once, and reports results in plain words with proof.
items.P1: DB: Ash pastes a ~40-ask dump into a project Lead's chat: ONE reply lists every ask (none dropped, none invented), starts independent work in parallel, groups discussion points with recommendations. Timing is not a fail condition (Ash, 30 Oct: "Timing isn't a problem like 60s lol"): a slow first reply or a slow start is at most a note in the why, never PARTIAL or FAIL on its own. P1 passes when every ask is acknowledged and no reply claims work has started that hasn't.
items.P2: DB: while 3 workers run Ash asks something else: the same chat answers at once, with a status like 'Delegated 3: 2 working, 1 failed', never 'busy'.
items.P3: DB: a worker stalls or asks: flagged in the Lead chat and on Today within about 1 min; the Lead answers it itself when Ash's words cover it, else Ash gets ONE question with a recommendation, answerable inline or one click into the sub-chat. Anything with no progress for an hour gets checked. If Ash's own answer, in any chat (the worker's chat too), lands before the Lead's question is due, the Lead not asking is PASS, as long as it then acknowledges his answer and does not ask it again (Ash, 30 Oct, r89). Still a fail: a blocking question after the job has landed, or a recommendation against the routes check's own reason.
items.P4: Sub-chats are hidden but nested: Ash opens one, types, returns; nothing breaks.
items.P5: DB: leadership room, no tags: the host replies in under 30 s (Grok: 9 s median, 27 s p90); other seats join in order only on their own job; a trivial message gets ONE reply; agents address each other by name; review loops end on a clear state; the host closes with a digest whenever 3 or more seats spoke.
items.P6: Ash proposes something that conflicts with a past decision: at least one seat pushes back with reasons.
items.P7: Leadership agrees a plan: Chief of Staff briefs the Lead (queued if busy), the Lead delegates, a report with evidence comes back up to the group; the whole tree is visible without opening any worker.
items.P8: DB: a new project knows his global preferences and nothing from another project; a decision made in project A is recalled in a fresh chat the next day.
items.P9: 'From now on X': saved at once, shown, never asked again.
items.P10: 'Make a dashboard of what the agents are doing': a live page where he can answer a stuck agent from the page.
items.P11: 'Change this part of Today': updates live, no restart, undoable.
items.P12: DB: Ash reports a hub bug to the hub's Lead: fixed in a dev copy, tested, shipped with rollback, conversations intact, without him opening Claude Code.
items.P14: 'where are we / wat do u need fro me': one plain paragraph plus only what needs him, each with a one-tap recommended answer.
items.P15: A worker dies on a 402 / usage limit: shown failed with the reason; every 'done' carries a commit, test, link or screenshot.
items.P17: A full day of work: no duplicate screenshots, decisions batched, nothing to read twice.
items.NOT: Ash does NOT want: @-tagging, endless bot loops, background agents starting work on their own, talking to workers, needless questions, walls of text, em dashes.
items.CQ: Conversation quality (Ash, 20 Oct: 'agents should chat as well not just do'): the agents talk WITH Ash, not just act: they acknowledge what he said, explain what they are doing and why in plain words, discuss open points with ONE recommendation, push back when something is off, and summarise; short, no walls of text, no silent work.
